label: Prospector Pell, late runs — identification as indictment

purpose.value: Pell performs identification as indictment: he lays the hero's hoard out in a row and names each piece by the home it came from — the 'dark shards' were always domestic magic, and now every one gets its provenance said aloud.

emotionalProgression.note: Slower now; each shard set down one at a time, named, no banter left in the lens work.
'Bowl. Toy. Fishing hook. Family portrait. Heating stone. That is your hoard, friend. Shall I grade the portrait?'

notes: The escalation endpoint for the shard arc: the patient re-identification of the greeting has become a row of objects and the homes they came from. The last honest attempt. The hero's reply will still be some variant of 'At last, the enemy respects me.' — that framing belongs to his side of the exchange (notes only), never to an NPC line. Never validate the hero's prophecy framing: there is no canon fact supporting 'the realms are evil', and that absence is itself the guard.
